messages:
tara: quick q — UX folks, product, and platform: should the Console show a live ‘handoff policy’ preview before enabling automatic fallback? want to avoid accidental mass rollouts.
james: yes. require a preview + dry-run toggle. show expected traffic split and estimated token delta. :eyes: 
maria: +1. also show last 24h error distribution and a small simulation of how many requests would match the trigger. make it easy to understand.
oliver: for the API shape we debated earlier, how about a compact policy DSL:
```json
{
  "on_error": "handoff",               // handoff | reject | throttle | cached_response
  "target_route": "redwood-lite",   // fallback route or model variant
  "threshold_pct": 5,                     // percent errors over window to trigger
  "window_sec": 300,                      // rolling window
  "min_traffic": 100,                     // only trigger if >= requests in window
  "audit": true,                          // record audit events and who enabled
  "dry_run": false                         // when true, only simulate
}
```
kevin: curious about the UX copy: if audit=true we should surface which user or service enabled the policy, and include a one-click revert. security likes the revert.
tara: agreed. also need a clear signal in dashboards: fallback_rate over time, correlated with latency and token spend. should be per-route and token-bucketed.
james: telemetry note — emit these events: `policy.evaluated`, `policy.triggered`, `policy.fallback_taken`, `policy.reverted`. each should include decision metadata and matched_rule_id. keeps audit simple.
maria: one more guard: automatic fallback should never change customer-visible model family unless explicitly allowed for private deployments. default should route to a compatible variant only (same architecture). we should show compatibility badge in preview.
oliver: implementation question: should we run policy evaluation client-side in the routing layer (fast) or a centralized policy service (easier to audit)? my vote: eval in the routing plane but stream evaluation logs to central audit stream. that gives low-latency decisions + audit.
kevin: yes but add sampling for full request dumps to keep costs down. sample 0.1% by default, configurable.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for experiment/hand-off-preview v.3 by tara at 1783001200 — monitoring enabled.
tara: for console: Add a small simulator widget: paste a short sample of recent requests or use last-N window, press "Run Simulation" and show how many would have fallen back. make dry-run default when someone creates a new auto-handoff policy.
james: UX nit — the preview should show both optimistic and conservative outcomes: optimistic = assumes no traffic spike; conservative = assume +20% error noise. show both numbers.
maria: on the audit trail, store: policy config, who changed it, timestamp, dry_run flag, simulation snapshot, and a checksum of the exact model variants used. make it exportable (CSV/JSON) for SOC reviews.
oliver: we should add an escape hatch API: POST /internal/policy/{id}/force-revert with admin auth. console shows that button but disabled unless you have admin rights.
kevin: last: quota interplay—if fallback route is a paid dedicated pool, warn about possible overages and surface estimated spend. Console should refuse to enable auto-handoff if it would breach a quota unless an override checkbox is ticked.
tara: love that. i'll mock a console flow and screens this afternoon. will include copy for warnings and the dry-run modal.
james: thanks everyone — next steps: tara will do mocks, oliver will prototype eval-in-plane streaming audit events, maria will write telemetry schema, kevin will draft quota blocking/override UX. check back here when you have PRs. :thumbsup:
